evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨文、金文用例
evidence.text: The database explains ancient 見 as 目 plus 卩, with 卩 a kneeling person and the eye emphasized for seeing. It reports oracle-bone uses for seeing and audience, and a use read as 獻 ‘offer sacrificial goods’; bronze uses include seeing, audience, and a passive auxiliary. It does not give a specimen-level date sequence on this page.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 見

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, quoting 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The received dictionary entry defines 見 as ‘視也’ and parses it as 从儿从目. Duan Yucai glosses the form as a person using the eyes and identifies it as a huiyi analysis. This later graph analysis does not independently establish details of the earlier oracle-bone forms.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and later annotation
evidence.title: 說文解字「見」

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.field: 字形演變；甲骨文、金文、楚系簡帛、小篆
evidence.text: The record indexes oracle-bone form 合集6790, bronze form 集成02612, Chu bamboo and silk forms, and seal script. Its explanation describes a human form with a prominent eye, meaning seeing with the eyes. The record does not provide a dated specimen sequence or explain every intermediate graphic transition.
evidence.title: 漢字「見」：字形演變

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK entry, Shuowen.org, Sinica character evolution entry and Xiaoxuetang rights/coverage guide. Search found a Commons oracle-style vector; its provenance and rights were checked. It is a modern drawing, not an artifact photograph.

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 見 oracle bone script 見字
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Commons oracle-style and bronze-style 見 vector file pages; both directly identify the graph and claim public-domain reuse for the vector representations. Other results were not selected because they were not identified as 見.

gaps: The checked pages do not establish a specimen-level earliest date or a fully dated sequence of seeing, audience, offering, and passive uses.

The reported oracle-bone use read as 獻 is a whole-graph borrowing claim separate from the graph’s person-and-eye formation. The source page asserts it, but this research did not retrieve inscription-level examples or independent comparative sound evidence. The pictured person’s name or pronunciation is not thereby established or required by the reported claim.

No evidence inspected here demonstrates corruption or independently traces the simplified 见 shape to a particular cursive exemplar. The graph’s ancient graphic development and the 見/见 standard correspondence should not be collapsed into a single dated sequence.

The Shuowen analysis of 儿 plus 目 is a received-form account; the CUHK analysis of 目 plus 卩 describes its interpretation of ancient forms. These are stage- and source-specific accounts, not evidence that the lower graph is phonetic.
Current Unihan readings were not verified: an official lookup attempt failed. No phonetic component is proposed, so no component-to-host sound comparison applies.

No queried Xiaoxuetang glyph image was selected. The Commons drawings were selected because their record pages directly identify the graph, describe the script style, give source attribution, and state reuse terms.

items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 見 in Shang oracle-script style. The form is described as combining an eye and a person.

items.selection_reason: Shows the source-described person-and-eye design associated with the ancient graph; the file page identifies the J20938 source example and states public-domain reuse for the vector.

limitations.text: These assets are modern vector redrawings of historical script styles, not photographs or direct facsimiles of the cited oracle-bone and bronze specimens. Captions should preserve that distinction.
Commons attributes the model examples to the Richard Sears Chinese Etymology data; the image descriptions do not provide specimen dates for those models.
